home.title: IPQuery · IP Geolocation
home.heroTitleAccent:
Look up any IP address,
get trustworthy country, city, and ASN
home.heroSubLong: Aggregates MaxMind GeoLite2, ip2region, and DB-IP using a field-complementary strategy. 100% self-hosted. Sub-100ms median latency.

features.title: One query, three sources
features.sub: Primary source first, backups fill the gaps. Each field is tagged with its source so you can decide.

sources.title: Multi-source merge
sources.sub: MaxMind / ip2region / DB-IP back each other up. Field coverage is far higher than single-source solutions.

coverage.title: IPv4 + IPv6 coverage
coverage.sub: Stored by range, not by IP. 8.3M+ ranges cover almost the entire routable internet.

speed.title: Sub-100ms
speed.sub: Spatial index ordered by range_size: smallest first. Median latency well below industry average.

steps.title: Three steps
steps.sub: No network downloads, no in-memory database. Just a single MySQL query.

s1.title: Send an IP
s1.sub: Form or HTTP call. Any IPv4/IPv6 address works.

s2.title: Match the range
s2.sub: Composite index sorted by range_size. The smallest matching CIDR wins in milliseconds.

s3.title: Get JSON back
s3.sub: Country, region, city, ISP, ASN. Each field carries its source.

code.title: Three lines of code
code.sub: Public endpoints need no auth. Signed-up users get API keys raising the rate limit to 60/min.

cta.title: Start using IPQuery
cta.sub: No credit card. Sign up for an API key and switch to production whenever you're ready.

home.heroSubtitle: Aggregating MaxMind / ip2region / DB-IP with daily ETL refresh

about.heading: A lightweight, self-hosted IP geolocation service
about.intro: Built for developers. Does one thing well: aggregate scattered free IP data sources behind one stable, auditable API.
about.storyP1: Existing IP lookup services are either expensive (per-QPS billing), stale (free sources rarely updated), or opaque (no field provenance means you can't judge trust).
about.storyP2: IPQuery flips that: free, self-hosted, transparent field sources. Daily ETL pipelines keep a single MySQL table fresh. A lookup is just a regular SQL query.

sources.title: Multi-source merge
sources.sub: Each field carries its source ( maxmind / ip2region / dbip ) for audit and traceability.

speed.title: Index-first
speed.sub: Composite index sorted by range_size — smallest first, avoiding full table scans over large ranges.

opensource.title: Open source
opensource.sub: MIT licensed. Audit the ETL, the query path, the scheduler — nothing hidden.

selfhosted.title: Fully self-hosted
selfhosted.sub: Data lives in your own database. API runs on your own server. User queries never leave your infrastructure.

stack.handlebars: Server-side templates. Zero client dependencies. Lean to the bone.

about.licenseBody: Source code is MIT licensed. Data files are downloaded and consumed under each upstream's own license terms (MaxMind / ip2region / DB-IP).

2024.title: First commit
2024.desc: Initial schema, MaxMind-only loader, and a Fastify server. Single-table design, one source.

2025.title: ip2region + DB-IP integration
2025.desc: Three-source merge strategy with field-level source tracking. Range-size index for sub-100ms lookups.

2026.title: Production-ready release
2026.desc: Auth, rate limiting, ETL scheduling, dashboard, multi-locale. Open-sourced under MIT.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.heading: A simple HTTP API
docs.subtitle: Public HTTP API, no auth required; sign up for an API key for higher rate limits.

endpoints.lookup: Lookup IP country / region / city / ISP / ASN
endpoints.lookupPath: Same, with IP as a path parameter
endpoints.stats: Last ETL run metadata (started / finished / status / merged records)

docs.authBody: Create an API key in the dashboard, then pass it via key= or Authorization: Bearer.
docs.responseBody: Successful responses are JSON. Missing fields are null. Each data field carries its source, naming the upstream it came from.
docs.authQueryNote: The ?key= form still works, but a key in the URL ends up in server logs, proxy logs and browser history. Prefer the Authorization header — it stays out of every log. Requests using ?key= receive a Deprecation header.
docs.rateLimitsBody: The public API is rate limited per source IP. Requests carrying an API key and requests without one share the same budget — a key authenticates you, it does not raise your limit. Web pages and static assets are not subject to this limit.

rateLimits.publicDesc: /healthz, /lookup and /stats share one counter, keyed by source IP. Anonymous requests and requests carrying an API key draw on the same budget.
rateLimits.keyedDesc: HTML pages, stylesheets and scripts are not rate limited. A single page load can pull a dozen resources, and sharing the API budget with them would turn ordinary browsing into a 429.
rateLimits.adminDesc: The admin panel polls live ETL progress, so it has its own, larger bucket and never consumes the public budget.

docs.rateLimitsScopeNote: Rate limiting is by path. Web pages and static assets are outside the public API budget. A route-level limit replaces the global limit for that route rather than adding to it, and the admin panel’s polling routes are budgeted separately from the public API.
